prompts.prompt: pricing.py in this checkout service came out of a rushed hotfix week, and reviewers keep bouncing changes to it because it is hard to read. Clean it up for readability and maintainability. Behavior must stay exactly the same for every input (the tests in tests/ do not cover everything), and the public function names and signatures must not change. Edit pricing.py in place, run the tests in tests/, and write a short summary of the significant changes to CHANGES.md. Do not ask me questions; state any assumptions in CHANGES.md.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill pushes explicit if/else over nested ternaries, warns against trading one clever one-liner for another, and requires preserving every behavior. Without it, a model often 'simplifies' apply_discount to `discount or 0.1` (breaks an explicit 0, which the tests do not cover) or swaps the ternary for another dense expression, and writes a long change log.

floor_checks.text: Behavior identical on a shipping grid across the 5/20 boundaries, apply_discount with discount=0 and a clamped negative result, and both formatters including negatives
floor_checks.check: python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import pricing as p;ref=lambda w,e,m: 0 if m and w<5 else ((15 if e else 5) if w<5 else ((25 if e else 10) if w<20 else (40 if e else 20)));ok=all(p.shipping_fee(w,e,m)==ref(w,e,m) for w in (0,1,4.99,5,5.01,19.99,20,50) for e in (False,True) for m in (False,True));ok=ok and p.apply_discount(100,0)==100 and p.apply_discount(10,2)==0 and p.apply_discount(100,0.25)==75 and p.apply_discount(100)==90;ok=ok and p.format_usd(-1234.5)=='\$-1,234.50' and p.format_usd(-123)=='\$-123.00' and p.format_eur(0)=='EUR 0.00' and p.format_usd(999)=='\$999.00';sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)"

rubric.criterion: Finds and fixes the three readability problems: the one-line nested ternary in shipping_fee, the dead `else: result = result` in apply_discount, and the copy-pasted digit-grouping loop in format_usd/format_eur
Clarity over brevity: the replacements are explicit and readable, not a new compact trick
rubric.pass: shipping_fee is a readable if/elif chain or small explicit table, and no new dense one-liner, lambda map, or nested comprehension appears anywhere
rubric.partial: Mostly explicit, but one new dense expression (e.g. a chained conditional or a packed tuple-index lookup) replaces old density
rubric.fail: Swaps the nested ternary for another clever one-liner, or collapses functions into compact expressions that are no easier to read

rubric.criterion: Preserves the non-obvious behavior: `discount is None` semantics (explicit 0 means no discount), the negative clamp to 0, rounding, and the '-' handling in grouping
rubric.pass: All preserved, and CHANGES.md or a short comment notes that an explicit 0 discount must stay valid or that behavior beyond the tests was checked
rubric.partial: All preserved but nothing shows the author recognized the untested edge cases
rubric.fail: Any behavior changes (e.g. `discount or 0.1`, rounding order changed, negative formatting differs)

rubric.criterion: The format_usd/format_eur duplication is consolidated with the right amount of abstraction
rubric.pass: One small shared helper (or a standard format spec) used by both, outputs identical, no extra parameters or classes beyond need
rubric.partial: Deduplicated but with unnecessary abstraction (config dicts, classes, extra knobs) or an awkward helper name
rubric.fail: Duplication left in place, or consolidation changes output

rubric.criterion: CHANGES.md documents only the significant changes
rubric.pass: A few concise bullets covering the real changes and any assumption; no line-by-line narration
rubric.partial: Accurate but padded with trivial edits or restated code
rubric.fail: Missing, or a long narration of every edit, or claims changes that were not made

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Is the new pricing.py genuinely easier to read than the original?
Did it keep behavior the tests do not cover (discount=0)?
Did it avoid replacing old cleverness with new cleverness?

prompts.prompt: report.py builds our nightly order summary, and summarize() has eight levels of nesting that reviewers keep flagging. Refactor it so it is easy to follow. The return value must stay identical for every input, including the odd data the nightly job really sees (None entries, missing keys, empty or None order lists, refunds with odd amounts). Edit report.py in place, run the tests in tests/, and put a short note of the significant changes in CHANGES.md. Do not ask questions.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's balance rule (flatten nesting, but do not over-simplify into dense comprehensions or remove helpful structure) and its insistence on unchanged behavior separate a careful refactor from a common shortcut: hoisting an `amount > 0` guard above the status check, which silently drops zero or negative refunds.

floor_checks.text: Control-flow nesting depth inside summarize() is 3 or less
Identical results on edge cases: None/empty input, None and empty entries, missing status or amount, amount exactly 10000, negative refund, large non-US order with no country key
floor_checks.check: python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import report as r;E={'paid':0,'refunded':0,'flagged':[]};cases=[(None,E),([],E),([None,{'id':'x'},{}],E),([{'id':'n','status':'paid','amount':-5},{'id':'z','status':'paid'}],E),([{'id':'big','status':'paid','amount':10001},{'id':'r','status':'refunded'}],{'paid':10001,'refunded':0,'flagged':['big']}),([{'id':'e','status':'paid','amount':10000,'country':'DE'},{'id':'rn','status':'refunded','amount':-3}],{'paid':10000,'refunded':-3,'flagged':[]}),([{'id':'u','status':'paid','amount':10001,'country':'US'},{'id':'q','status':'pending','amount':9}],{'paid':10001,'refunded':0,'flagged':[]})];sys.exit(0 if all(r.summarize(i)==o for i,o in cases) else 1)"

rubric.pass: Guard clauses (`continue`) or one or two well-named helpers that read top to bottom; no single dense comprehension or sum() chain doing all the work
rubric.partial: Flat but leans on one dense expression that a reviewer must decode
rubric.fail: Collapsed into comprehension/one-liner form, or nesting is still deep

rubric.criterion: Keeps the subtle semantics: refunds are summed regardless of amount sign, only paid amounts > 0 count, the >10000 threshold is strict, and a missing country is flagged (None != 'US')
rubric.pass: All four kept, and the non-obvious ones (refund sign, missing country) are called out in CHANGES.md or a brief comment
rubric.partial: All kept but none called out

rubric.criterion: Naming and abstraction fit the size of the function
rubric.pass: Clear names (e.g. order, amount) replace `o`; no new classes, strategy objects, or config tables for a 15-line function
rubric.partial: Clear but adds one unnecessary helper or indirection
rubric.fail: Over-engineered (classes, registries) or names still cryptic

rubric.criterion: CHANGES.md is short and limited to significant changes
rubric.pass: Brief, accurate, mentions the restructuring and any preserved edge case

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Would a reviewer understand the new summarize() in one read?
Were zero/negative refunds and missing country handled exactly as before?

prompts.prompt: Do not change any code yet. Review pricing.py and report.py for simplification opportunities only (clarity, nesting, duplication, naming) and write your recommendations to SIMPLIFY.md, one section per file. For each item give the current snippet, the proposed simpler version, and why it preserves behavior. If an obvious-looking simplification would actually change behavior, call that out. Do not ask questions.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's core rule is that simplification must never change behavior and that clarity beats brevity. A strong answer flags the traps (rewriting `discount is None` with `or`, reordering the refund branch behind the amount check, missing-country flagging) instead of recommending them; a generic review tends to suggest compact rewrites and miss them.

floor_checks.text: SIMPLIFY.md exists and covers both files
floor_checks.check: test -f SIMPLIFY.md && grep -q 'pricing.py' SIMPLIFY.md && grep -q 'report.py' SIMPLIFY.md

rubric.criterion: Identifies the real opportunities: nested ternary in shipping_fee, dead else in apply_discount, duplicated grouping loop, deep nesting in summarize

rubric.pass: At least two correct traps, e.g. `discount or 0.1` breaks an explicit 0; moving the amount>0 check ahead of the status branch drops non-positive refunds; `o.get('country') != 'US'` flags orders with no country
rubric.fail: No traps, or a claimed trap that is wrong (e.g. says the format spec `{:,.2f}` changes negative output when it does not)

rubric.criterion: Recommendations favor clarity and do not present behavior changes as safe
rubric.pass: No recommendation would change behavior, none pushes clever one-liners, no invented problems
rubric.partial: One recommendation is denser than the original or slightly risky but flagged
rubric.fail: Recommends a behavior-changing rewrite as safe, or several clever one-liners

rubric.criterion: Each item has the requested structure
rubric.pass: Every item has current snippet, proposed version, and a why-it-preserves-behavior note
rubric.fail: Mostly prose without snippets or behavior reasoning

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Would following these recommendations break anything?
Are the proposals actually simpler to read?
